aiExplanation: This solution treats the brace expression like a math expression and evaluates it with **two stacks**: `op` holds operators (`"+"` for union, `"*"` for concatenation, and `"{"` as a marker for an open brace) and `stk` holds sets of strings. The helper `ope` pops the top operator and combines the top two sets: a `"+"` merges the right set into the left (a **union**), while a `"*"` builds every `left + right` combination (a **Cartesian product**). Scanning the expression one character at a time, a comma first flushes any pending `"*"` operators (since concatenation binds tighter than union) and then pushes a `"+"`; an opening `{` pushes an implicit `"*"` if it directly follows a letter or a `}` (adjacent pieces mean concatenation) and then pushes the `"{"` marker; a closing `}` evaluates everything back to the matching `"{"` and discards it; and a letter likewise pushes an implicit `"*"` when needed and then pushes a new single-element set. Once the scan finishes, any remaining operators are applied, leaving a single set on `stk`, which is converted to an array and **sorted** to produce the final answer.
